articles.body:
Justin Jefferson has his former quarterback back in the building.

The Minnesota Vikings acquired Kirk Cousins from the Las Vegas Raiders on Tuesday ahead of the deadline, reuniting him with Jefferson. Following the trade, Jefferson praised Cousins' leadership.

"It's just kind of a joy to hear him take over and be a leader in the meeting room, on the field," Jefferson told reporters Thursday. "It's definitely a cool little situation, for sure."

Cousins played for the Vikings from 2018 to 2023, throwing to Jefferson for four seasons. Jefferson had the best seasons of his career with Cousins throwing to him, including in 2022, when he had 1,809 yards and eight touchdowns.

Cousins likewise had his best seasons in Minnesota when his top target was Jefferson, and they'll look to pick up where they left off.

Cousins signed with the Raiders over the offseason after two years with the Atlanta Falcons, and he's had a strong start to the year despite Las Vegas' struggles. He's thrown for the fifth-most yards (2,340) and the second-most touchdowns (20).

Jefferson, meanwhile, has had a down year amid what has been a slow start to the year offensively for the Vikings.

With Cousins now under center again, the 6-2 Vikings will try to get their offense going to keep up with their outstanding defense. If all of that comes together, Minnesota will have all the makings of a Super Bowl contender.

articles.title: Puka Nacua Injury Update, Latest News on Rams WR's Status and Return Timeline Amid Knee Issue
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Rams will be without wide receiver Puka Nacua for the foreseeable future.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams will be without wide receiver Puka Nacua for the foreseeable future.

The NFC West team placed the playmaker on injured reserve because of his MCL injury. What's more, head coach Sean McVay said his expectation is Nacua will miss "extended time."

This is a change in direction for the Rams, as McVay initially told reporters that even though the wide receiver was going to miss "a significant period of time," the plan was not to place him on IR due to "semantics with the roster."

Losing Nacua is quite the blow for Los Angeles seeing how Davante Adams is already sidelined with a hamstring injury.

Nacua's injury happened during Sunday's win over the Washington Commanders, although he still finished with a head-turning 14 receptions for 150 yards and one touchdown on 19 targets. Through seven games this season, he has 70 catches for 715 yards and four touchdowns.

With both of Matthew Stafford's top receivers sidelined, the Rams will likely rely on the combination of Tutu Atwell, Konata Mumpfield and CJ Daniels at the position. Tight end Tyler Higbee will likely see plenty of targets as well, although even he missed practice Thursday because of an illness.

Ultimately, the Rams are not going to be nearly as dangerous with both Nacua and Adams out.

Nacua is one of the best wide receivers in the league and someone Stafford routinely targets double-digit amounts of time per game. There will be more pressure on the rushing attack to carry the offense with the two top playmakers sidelined, and there is also little room for error in the NFC standings.

After all, Los Angeles is three games behind the San Francisco 49ers in the NFC West at 5-4 and on the outside of the playoff picture looking in at this point. The Green Bay Packers have the final wild-card spot at 6-3 and will face the Rams in Week 12 while Nacua is still out.

With remaining games against the Packers, 49ers and Kansas City Chiefs, as well as two against the Seattle Seahawks, there is a real chance the Rams will miss the playoffs.

And those chances are much higher with Nacua not on the field.

articles.body: A reunion between Tyreek Hill and the Kansas City Chiefs might sound exciting to fans who remember his explosive partnership with Patrick Mahomes. But bringing the wide receiver back to Arrowhead could create problems that go far beyond football. Hill's serious knee injury, questions about his long-term fitness and a controversial off-field history have made the possibility difficult to ignore. With Kansas City looking for more firepower in its receiving group, the temptation to bring back a familiar superstar may exist. However, the Chiefs could have compelling reasons to look elsewhere.Tyreek Hill's injury raises major concerns for a Chiefs reunionHill's familiarity with Andy Reid's offensive system makes him an attractive name whenever Kansas City's receiving needs come into discussion. He spent six seasons with the Chiefs, building a dangerous connection with Mahomes before joining the Miami Dolphins in 2022.His speed and ability to turn short passes into explosive plays helped make him one of the NFL's most feared receivers. Yet his current physical condition raises serious questions about whether he could deliver the same impact.Hill suffered a devastating knee injury last September, involving torn cruciate ligaments and a dislocated kneecap. Such an injury can demand a long and difficult recovery, particularly for a player whose biggest strength depends on acceleration, speed and sudden changes of direction.Reports of lingering muscle weakness have added to concerns about his progress. At 32, Hill would also face the challenge of returning to elite form after major surgery.For the Chiefs, this would be more than a familiar player returning to a familiar offence. Hill's history away from the field could make a reunion an even more difficult decision for Kansas City.Hill pleaded guilty to domestic abuse by strangulation in 2015 involving his then-pregnant partner. More recently, a civil jury found him liable on multiple counts of assault in a separate case. articles.title: Mike Tomlin Explains Why He Stepped Down as Steelers HC After 19 Seasons in New Video
articles.summary: Former Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin explained his decision to step down from the position after the 2025 season.
articles.body:
Former Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin explained his decision to step down from the position after the 2025 season.

"Football is bigger than all of us and I never took myself so seriously that I thought that I was immune from that," Tomlin said during a Tuesday appearance on the Not Just Football podcast. "I never wanted to stay too long. Also, there's a cumulative component to coaching. I had 19 years of baggage and sometimes your teams have to carry your bags. I just thought that we had the making of a really good team, a team that's capable of competing for and winning a championship."

"But when I really started thinking about it, my bags might slow that down," he added. "I thought that guys like him and T.J. and others were deserving of the support that comes with transition. The optimism that comes with new regimes. I saw it in Tampa. I want that for those guys, even if it means it doesn't happen with me. I've seen everything this game has to offer. I've had the confetti rain down on me more than once. I want that for him, I want that for T.J. Watt. They're deserving. Even if it means it doesn't include me, I'm okay with that."

Tomlin served as the Steelers' head coach for 19 seasons from 2007-25.

He was the longest-tenured coach in the NFL until he announced that he was stepping down "after much thought and reflection" on Jan. 13.

Tomlin compiled a 193-114-2 record in Pittsburgh, as the team never finished with a losing record during any year he spent patrolling the sidelines. The Steelers made 13 playoff appearances under Tomlin, capturing a Super Bowl title during the 2008 season.

Pittsburgh struggled to make deep playoff runs near the end of his time with the organization, as the team has lost six consecutive postseason games.

The Steelers also finished at 10-7 before getting eliminated in the Wild Card round of the playoffs during each of Tomlin's final three seasons.

While he still experienced plenty of success during his time in Pittsburgh, he decided that the team needed a new voice in the locker room.

The Steelers are now in the midst of their first season with Mike McCarthy as head coach, currently sitting atop the AFC North standings with a 6-2 record.

As for Tomlin, he's been operating as a football analyst for NBC Sports.

articles.title: Rams place WR Puka Nacua on IR with knee, turf toe injuries
articles.summary: Nacua will now miss at least 4 weeks after sustaining multiple knee sprains and a turf toe injury last week.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams have placed Puka Nacua on injured reserve, the team announced Thursday. The move will sideline the receiver for at least four games after he suffered multiple injuries last week.

In a connected move, the Rams have signed receiver Brennan Presley to the active roster from the practice squad, and signed WR Tyler Scott to the practice squad.

Nacua sustained the injuries late in the Rams' win over the Washington Commanders on Sunday. He was later diagnosed with MCL and PCL sprains on his right knee as well as a turf toe injury.

Head coach Sean McVay told reporters on Wednesday that Nacua will miss "a significant period of time" with the injuries. McVay initially said that the receiver would not go on IR due to "some semantics with the roster," but that appears to have changed.

By being on IR, the earliest that Nacua could return is against the Dallas Cowboys on Dec. 20.

Nacua, who missed two games early in the season with a hip injury, has had a strong 2026 season up to this point. In seven games, he's caught 70 receptions for 715 yards and four touchdowns. The Commanders' game was his most productive of the season before the injuries, as the receiver picked up 14 catches for 150 yards and a touchdown.

Nacua joins the Rams' other key receiver, Davante Adams, on IR; Adams has been there since Week 6 with a ruptured hamstring. McVay said Wednesday that he is hoping for Adams to return in Week 13, meaning it will still be a couple of weeks of playing with a shrunken receiver core.

articles.title: Chargers GM Talks NFL Trade Deadline, Reveals Untouchable Players Despite 0-8 Record
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Chargers didn't finalize any trades prior to this year's deadline on Nov. 10 despite losing their first eight games.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Chargers didn't finalize any trades prior to this year's deadline on Nov. 10 despite losing their first eight games.

On Thursday, Chargers general manager Joe Hortiz spoke with reporters for the first time post-deadline, explaining why the team didn't make moves and noting players who were untouchable.

"I've been on the phone since Week 3 talking to teams," Hortiz told reporters, per ESPN's Lindsey Thiry . "They've inquired about players' availabilities. I've said, 'Hey, this player, no, we're not trading.' Would we consider something? Yes, but it would have to be a good package for us to move them. No one put together any packages that blew us away or that inspired us to continue."

The Chargers had a deal in place to send linebacker Daiyan Henley to the Denver Broncos for a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick. However, per ESPN's Jeff Legwold , the Broncos called the deal off after discovering an issue with one of Henley's knees during the physical.

Hence, the Bolts will hit the second half of the season with the same roster. Hortiz made it very clear the Chargers weren't trading some players, though, naming five in particular: quarterback Justin Herbert, wide receiver Ladd McConkey, left tackle Joe Alt, safety Derwin James Jr. and cornerback Tarheeb Still.

"There were some players that you're just not going to trade," Hortiz said. "I'm not trading Justin [Herbert], right? No one ever called on Justin, but I'm not trading Justin. I'm not trading Ladd [McConkey]. I'm not trading Joe [Alt]. I'm not trading Derwin [James Jr.]. It's just not happening. Tarheeb Still, these players that have futures with us. And a lot of those guys, people didn't call on them."

The Chargers won 11 games and made the playoffs each of the last two seasons under head coach Jim Harbaugh. Hopes were high for 2026, especially after L.A. brought in former Miami Dolphins head coach and San Francisco 49ers offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel, who had a heavy hand in some successful and explosive offenses at previous stops.

However, this season has gone as poorly as possible. Not only are the Chargers last in scoring (15.1 PPG), but their defense has taken a big hit, with the team allowing 27.4 PPG (28th in the NFL). Opponents have outscored Los Angeles by 98 points, and five of their eight losses have been by 12 or more points.

There are certainly many questions about how Los Angeles can possibly regroup and fare better in 2027. In the meantime, though, the Chargers must finish out 2026, beginning Monday evening when they visit the Baltimore Ravens.

articles.summary: The Philadelphia Eagles are reportedly waiving veteran wideout Hollywood Brown, according to reporter Jordan Schultz.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles are reportedly waiving veteran wideout Hollywood Brown, according to reporter Jordan Schultz .

He may be an option for teams that didn't address the wideout position ahead of this week's trade deadline but have a need there, like the Pittsburgh Steelers, or teams suddenly struggling with depth at the position, like the Los Angeles Rams or Indianapolis Colts.

Brown, 29, failed to make much impact for the Eagles despite starters DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks each missing several games this season, pulling down just five catches for 63 yards in four games.

He once appeared to be a burgeoning star, registering 91 catches for 1,008 yards and six scores in the 2021 season with the Baltimore Ravens. But since leaving Baltimore he's been more of a bit player in tenures with the Arizona Cardinals (2022-23) and Kansas City Chiefs (2024-25).

A return to Kansas City might have made some sense before the team traded for Josh Downs this week.

At this point, the Steelers and Rams are the two potential playoff teams who have the greatest need for receiving help. Pittsburgh surprisingly sat out the trade deadline, though the eventual returns of Michael Pittman Jr. and Roman Wilson may have played a part in that thinking.

The Rams, meanwhile, are in dire straits at the position, with both Davante Adams and Puka Nacua on injured reserve. Getting Matthew Stafford another weapon would make sense, with Konata Mumpfield (11 catches for 162 yards and a touchdown) currently his top option at receiver.

At this stage in his career, Brown isn't a game-changer, but it wouldn't be surprising if he picked up with a new team rather quickly.

articles.title: Does Jayden Daniels have a girlfriend? What his mother has revealed about the Commanders QB’s private life
articles.summary: Jayden Daniels has not said he is dating anyone.
articles.body: Jayden Daniels has not said he is dating anyone. The Washington Commanders quarterback, 25, has no confirmed relationship, no public partner and no Instagram posts that point to one. His mother, Regina Jackson, has said plenty about the subject, though. On Amazon Prime’s “The Money Game,” she joked that women chasing her son will have to get past her first. Rumors linking him to USC basketball star JuJu Watkins have floated around, but neither player has confirmed anything. For now, Daniels’ love life stays a blank, and his mother seems happy to keep guard.Jayden Daniels girlfriend status: no confirmed relationshipAs of mid-November 2026, Daniels has not confirmed a girlfriend. Nothing on his Instagram account points to a partner, and he has not talked about one in interviews. That stands out a little for a quarterback whose profile has grown fast since he joined Washington in 2024. Plenty of players his age share their relationships online. Daniels does not, and the injuries he has dealt with have kept most of the conversation on his health and availability instead.The one name that keeps coming up is JuJu Watkins.Fans tied the two together after a viral handshake between them, a moment Sports Illustrated also covered. Neither has said they are a couple. Without a word from either side, the talk stays talk. The rumor has no photo, no post and no quote from either camp behind it. A handshake is not a relationship, and treating it like one is a stretch.His past is just as quiet. Daniels has never named an ex or discussed a previous relationship in public. So is he single? Nobody outside his circle can say for sure. His mother’s comments lean that way, but she has not spelled it out, and a joke on a streaming show is thin evidence for anyone’s relationship status.Regina Jackson on the women chasing her sonJackson has never been shy about her role as gatekeeper. On “The Money Game,” she described the women she imagines lining up for her son, and Outkick carried her full answer:“Girls… them girls. Some girl out here, she’s got a Jayden Daniels wall and her mama says, ‘Hey honey, you’re going to be the one to get him.’ And I know that sounds crazy, but I guarantee there’s someone who’s trying to get their hooks into Jayden Daniels. So thank god he got a mama like me because it ain’t happening,” she said.It is a joke, and she delivers it like one. But a parent’s joke still says something about how a family handles fame. Daniels is 25, the starting quarterback of a team its city follows closely, and the people closest to him seem to have made privacy the default. A mother playing bouncer fits that.Jackson also shows up for his games and stays in his corner whether the result is good or bad.Daniels has given no sign he plans to change course. Football is where he has chosen to put his energy, and nothing public suggests that has changed. articles.title: Watch Jameis Winston's Funny 'Who Let the Dogs Out' Hard Count in Video from Giants vs. Commanders
articles.summary: New York Giants quarterback Jameis Winston took a unique approach with his hard count during the team's 24-21 loss to the Washington Commanders on Thursday night.
articles.body:
New York Giants quarterback Jameis Winston took a unique approach with his hard count during the team's 24-21 loss to the Washington Commanders on Thursday night.

As the Giants attempted to draw Washington offsides on fourth down in the fourth quarter of the contest, Winston shouted "Who let the dogs out" at the line of scrimmage as part of his elongated cadence.

The move was ultimately unsuccessful, as the Giants were given a delay of game penalty and forced to punt.

J.J. McCarthy currently serves as New York's starting signal-caller, although head coach John Harbaugh has routinely deployed the team's second-string passer for quarterback sneaks in short-yardage situations.

Winston, who's listed at 6'4" and 231 pounds, picked up 11 first downs on 18 rush attempts across seven games heading into Thursday's action.

Still, the Giants decided not to snap the ball on fourth down at their own 11-yard line.

New York held a 21-17 lead midway through the fourth quarter of Thursday's NFC East clash, although Washington moved in front following Stefon Diggs' 32-yard touchdown reception.

On the Giants' ensuing drive, McCarthy was picked off by Commanders cornerback Rasul Douglas to end the team's hopes of a late comeback.

With the defeat, New York dropped to 5-3-1.

articles.title: Commanders-Giants: Jameis Winston attempts to draw Washington offside with rendition of 'Who Let the Dogs Out'
articles.summary: Jameis Winston is going to do Jameis Winston things from time to time.
articles.body:
Jameis Winston didn't start for the New York Giants in "Thursday Night Football," but he sure made an impression.

The veteran quarterback had a few cameos in relief of J.J. McCarthy during a 24-21 loss to the Washington Commanders , including when the Giants were facing a fourth-and-1 deep in their own territory with less than four minutes left and a 21-17 lead. New York brought out the offense and it soon became clear the hope was to draw Washington offside.

It began with the usual tricks, like fake hard counts and players in motion. Then the Prime Video cameras caught Winston singing "Who Let the Dogs Out" by Baha Men.

Yes, really. It didn't work, as the Commanders stayed on their side of the line of scrimmage.

The Giants took a delay of game penalty that pushed them back to their 7-yard line and punted out of their own end zone. Punter Jordan Stout sent the ball 68 yards downfield, with the Commanders taking over on their own 37-yard line.

New York's defense held after that, with safety Ar'Darius Washington picking off Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels, but a subsequent three-and-out gave Washington the ball back. A 32-yard touchdown pass from Daniels to Stefon Diggs put the Commanders ahead, and a Rasul Douglas interception ended the game .

articles.title: NFL Playoff Picture 2026-27, Standings, Bracket Scenarios After Giants vs. Commanders
articles.summary: Week 10 of the NFL season is here, and with it comes a handful of divisional matchups that are bound to shake up the standings.
articles.body:
Week 10 of the NFL season is here, and with it comes a handful of divisional matchups that are bound to shake up the standings.

The week kicked off on Thursday with an NFC East clash between the New York Giants and the Washington Commanders. The Commanders desperately needed a win, and they got it to keep their playoff hopes alive.

Ahead of the rest of the matchups on Sunday and Monday, here's a look at the updated standings and playoff picture.

Jacksonville Jaguars (6-2, Lead AFC South)

Pittsburgh Steelers (6-2, Lead AFC North)

There was no change at the top of the AFC in Week 9, and the Buffalo Bills remain in control of both the division and the conference after Monday's win over the Minnesota Vikings.

The Broncos are rolling after winning their fifth straight game, but the Chiefs aren't far behind. The Jaguars are sitting comfortably atop a weak AFC South, while the Steelers now have the same record as the Bengals after Cincinnati won its fourth consecutive game, with Pittsburgh on a bye week.

The Chiefs and Bengals are still very much in the hunt for their respective division titles, but the Patriots' odds took a hit as they lost to the Green Bay Packers last week.

Sunday's game between the Steelers and Bengals will be the game to watch this week.

There is a pretty clear separation between the top and bottom halves of the AFC, though it's fair to say the Cleveland Browns are still in the hunt, especially with Deshaun Watson back this week.

The Raiders will be interesting to watch since they traded Kirk Cousins and promoted rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza to the starter. Perhaps a new quarterback can spark a late-season run for Las Vegas, but it's hard to imagine that will happen.

With Lamar Jackson on the injured reserve, the Ravens likely won't be able to overcome a 4-5 start, while the Texans are just hoping to go on a magical run as they did a year ago.

For the rest of the AFC, it's time to start preparing for the draft.

San Francisco 49ers (7-1, Lead NFC West)

The Niners held their spot atop the NFC this week after bouncing back from their first loss of the season.

The Bears jumped the Vikings for the top of the NFC North after Minnesota's ugly loss to the Bills, and Chicago is looking more and more like a Super Bowl contender each week.

The Giants' spot at the top of the NFC East is mostly a product of playing in a bad division, but nonetheless, New York is playoff-bound at the moment.

Each team in the NFC North is separated by one game or less, so the Panthers have no room for error against the Saints this week.

As of right now, it looks like the entire NFC North is going to be competing in the playoffs, which would be a first for the NFL. The Seattle Seahawks and Los Angeles Rams are both still hanging around, though.

The Seahawks' Super Bowl defense hasn't gone the way they hoped, but they're still in the mix. The Rams, meanwhile, seem to be on the right track after a rough start to the year.

Still, both teams have lots of work to do to break the strong hold the NFC North has on the playoff race.

The entire NFC South is up for grabs given how weak it has been this year, and the Saints can take first place from the Panthers with a win this week.

The NFC East is likewise still anyone's game, though it's fair to assume the Eagles are out of the mix with quarterback Jalen Hurts done for the year. Thursday's game was a must-win for the Commanders, and they're firmly back in the race for the NFC East.

articles.title: Commanders Beat Giants, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Jayden Daniels, McCarthy, Top Players
articles.summary: The Washington Commanders defeated the host New York Giants 24-21 on Thursday evening in an NFC East matchup.
articles.body:
The Washington Commanders defeated the host New York Giants 24-21 on Thursday evening in an NFC East matchup.

The Giants were 1.5-point favorites, per FanDuel Sportsbook , but the Commanders won after wide receiver Stefon Diggs' 32-yard touchdown catch with 57 seconds left and Washington cornerback Rasul Douglas' game-sealing interception on the Giants' final drive.

Here's a look at the box score, which includes some top fantasy performers such as Giants tight end Isaiah Likely and running back Cam Skattebo as well as Diggs.

Here's a look at some big moments from the game.

Diggs' Game-Winning TD; Douglas' Game-Sealing INT

The Commanders got the ball with 1:46 remaining in regulation down four in front of a raucous MetLife Stadium crowd and against a defense that ended the previous two drives with interceptions.

However, Washington only needed 49 seconds to take the lead. Wideout Treylon Burks drew a 33-yard pass interference penalty on cornerback Deonte Banks. Two plays netted Washington six yards, setting up 3rd-and-4.

Diggs then made the play of the game, beating cornerback Dru Phillips on a slant pattern and running into the end zone for the score.

The Giants still had three timeouts and 48 seconds left.

The drive got off to a great start when New York QB J.J. McCarthy found wide receiver Malachi Fields for a 21-yard gain, putting the Giants on the Washington 48. However, two incomplete passes followed, and then on 3rd-and-10, McCarthy fired a pass downfield in the face of an oncoming rush in hopes of finding wide receiver Malik Nabers. Douglas got the ball instead, and the game was over.

Giants Snatch Defeat From Jaws of Victory Despite 3 4th-Quarter Stops

The Giants' defense was sensational on its first three fourth quarter drives, forcing a turnover-on-downs and then coming away with a pair of interceptions courtesy of safety Jevon Holland and Ar'Darius Washington.

Holland's pick was particularly huge, as Washington had a 1st-and-10 from the Giants' 24-yard line. Daniels looked for tight end Chig Okonkwo, but Holland had another idea.

Washington's pick set the Giants up on the Commanders' 46-yard line with 2:15 left.

Two Skattebo runs gave the Giants seven yards, but then New York curiously called for a McCarthy keeper around the end as opposed to giving it to Skattebo or throwing it for a first down to effectively end the game.

The slow-developing play lost New York two yards, and the Giants opted to punt. However, punter Jordan Stout, who has been excellent all season, did not get a good one off, and his effort went just 12 yards.

That led to Washington's final drive and New York's failed last-gasp effort.

Ultimately, it felt like the Giants played not to lose. And simply put, the G-Men made too many mistakes.

Daniels, Styles Showcase Why They Are Franchise Cornerstones

Daniels proved once again why he's one of the league's most electric talents when everything is rolling. Although he threw a pair of fourth-quarter picks, he rallied back when it mattered most for the W.

Ultimately, Daniels threw for three touchdown passes. They were all on third down, and they all game at crucial times.

Of note, Daniels found rookie wideout Antonio Williams for six just after the midway point of the third quarter.

As for rookie linebacker Sonny Styles, the No. 7 overall pick in the 2026 draft, he proved once again why he'll be a force to be reckoned with for years. Styles finished with 13 tackles (five solo) and took down McCarthy on his aforementioned third-down keeper.

The best free agent pickup in the NFL this year is perhaps the Kansas City Chiefs' acquisition of running back Kenneth Walker III, but one can argue that Likely is second.

The ex-Baltimore Raven has been sensational, and he added another great game to his Giant resume on Thursday with nine catches and 127 yards.

His biggest play was a 66-yard TD to put the Giants in the lead midway through the fourth quarter. Much credit goes to McCarthy, who fired a dime through the defense for the score.

Commanders Execute a Pair of Clutch Red Zone Plays

Washington got it done in crucial spots.

First, Daniels hit tight end Ben Sinnott for a touchdown on 3rd-and-goal from the five-yard line with five seconds left in the first half. The PAT made it 10-7, Commanders.

Second, Commanders linebacker Frankie Luvu punched the ball away from Nabers late in the third quarter with Big Blue at the Washington 16-yard line down 17-14. Washington safety Jeremy Reaves recovered the ball.

If New York recovered, the Giants would have faced a third-and-long, but they likely would have had a short field goal attempt at worst.

Talk persisted before the trade deadline that the Giants were in the market for a running back, with the team even making a declined offer for Indianapolis Colts RB Jonathan Taylor, per ESPN's Jordan Raanan .

In his first post-deadline game, Skattebo shined by getting some tough yards between the tackles and amassing 122 yards from scrimmage and two touchdowns overall, leading to a pair of celebratory backflips.

Skattebo scored the Giants' first TD to cap a 16-play, 72-yard drive for an early 6-3 lead:

In the third quarter, Skattebo took a toss and ran for a 13-yard score. A PAT gave them a 14-10 edge.

Giants rookie kicker Dominic Zvada missed 5-of-22 field goals going into the evening, and he misfired on his sixth in the first quarter when he pulled a 33-yard field goal wide left to cap New York's second drive.

Zvada also kicked the ball out-of-bounds after the Giants went up 21-17. Or more specifically, he kicked the ball off near the sideline, but Commanders returner Luke McCaffrey smartly touched the ball with his feet out-of-bounds, putting Washington at its own 40-yard line.

The ensuing Washington drive led to an interception, but still, this was a difficult night overall for a kicker that's shown great potential and a big leg but needs to be more consistent.

The 5-3-1 Giants still lead the NFC East by two in the loss column, but this one stings, especially considering New York had a 93.2 percent chance to win after Daniels' second interception, per ESPN . Alas, a three-and-out, a bad punt, a worse penalty, a long TD pass and a failed final attempt sealed the deal.

They'll now have a mini-bye and welcome the AFC South-leading Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday, Nov. 22 at 4:25 p.m. ET.

As for the Commanders, their season is saved. A defeat would have (a) put them at 2-6-1 and (b) lost them the head-to-head tiebreaker with the Giants. Instead, they are 3-5-1 and own the tiebreaker now.

A tough battle awaits, though, at home vs. MVP candidate Joe Burrow and the 6-2 Cincinnati Bengals on Monday, Nov. 23.

articles.summary: Old faces in new places will define Week 10 of the NFL after the league's trade deadline came and went.
articles.body:
Old faces in new places will define Week 10 of the NFL after the league's trade deadline came and went.

Quarterback Kirk Cousins is back with the Minnesota Vikings. Wide receiver Keenan Allen is back on the West Coast, albeit with the San Francisco 49ers. Josh Downs provides Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs with a new offensive weapon. The Jacksonville Jaguars beefed up their defense with the additions of safety Jessie Bates III and defensive tackle Jordan Davis.

These debuts for new teams are only the start of the stories coming out of Week 10.

As always, Bleacher Report NFL analysts Brent Sobleski , Kris Knox , and Moe Moton are following the action to break down the biggest stories and most pressing questions emerging from each contest.

Washington Commanders at New York Giants

Did the Washington Commanders Actually Save Their Season?

After tying the New York Giants in Week 5, the Washington Commanders ensured Thursday's rematch ended differently.

The Commanders played aggressively, rallied to win late in the fourth quarter and improved to 3-5-1.

The victory was absolutely necessary to ensure the Giants didn't run away with the NFC East. Now, the Commanders remain within striking distance of the division leader. However, Washington still trails by two games and its upcoming schedule likely portends more week-to-week inconsistency.

The Cincinnati Bengals bring the league's best passing attack to town next weekend to face Washington's bottom-five pass defense. The Commanders should then be favored against the Arizona Cardinals and Tennessee Titans over the following two weeks. After that, they close the regular season with a difficult five-game stretch against the Houston Texans, Atlanta Falcons, Minnesota Vikings, Jacksonville Jaguars and Dallas Cowboys.

Yes, the Commanders kept their season alive. But a slow demise is likely forthcoming.

Washington Commanders' New Big-Play Threats in Passing Game

Ultimately, quarterback Jayden Daniels found Stefon Diggs for the game-winning 32-yard touchdown pass with under a minute remaining in regulation. However, the Commanders wouldn't have been in that position without tight end Ben Sinnott and rookie wide receiver Antonio Williams providing big plays earlier.

Entering Thursday's contest, Sinnott had caught one pass for six yards. The 2024 second-round draft pick hadn't caught more than three passes or provided over 36 receiving yards in any contest during his first two-plus seasons. He set career highs Thursday with four catches for 42 yards, including a touchdown grab.

Meanwhile, Williams continued to show his burst and ability to create after the catch on a 31-yard touchdown reception.

Terry McLaurin and Dyami Brown may be on injured reserve, but the Commanders have two young players filling the void.

Can New York Giants RB Cam Skattebo Do Enough to Answer Critics?

The New York Giants were active in the running back market prior to Tuesday's trade deadline. Ultimately, the organization didn't land Jonathan Taylor or any other option.

Cam Skattebo was forced to answer the bell on Thursday. He did so with 122 yards from scrimmage and a pair of touchdowns. Plus, he consistently stuck his nose in pass protection to help quarterback J.J. McCarthy.

Skattebo has now posted two straight appearances with 120 or more scrimmage yards. The second-year back will never be as explosive or dynamic as Taylor. However, he can be an adequate-to-quality starter if he's fully committed to serving as the hammer within the Giants offense.

Isaiah Likely Shows No. 1-Target Potential

Malik Nabers is the Giants' top wide receiver, but tight end Isaiah Likely made the big play Thursday to give New York a fourth-quarter lead.

McCarthy targeted Likely on 11 different occasions. The tight end responded with a career-best 127 receiving yards, including the all-important 66-yard touchdown connection.

When John Harbaugh served as the Baltimore Ravens' head coach, Mark Andrews was Lamar Jackson's favorite target. Likely could certainly be that for McCarthy and possibly Jaxson Dart upon his return.

Traded players will be in the spotlight during Sunday's action, but some players who stayed put will also be under extra scrutiny.

Case in point: this year's No. 1 overall pick, Fernando Mendoza, is expected to make his first NFL start following Kirk Cousins' trade to the Minnesota Vikings.

Meanwhile, the Indianapolis Colts chose to keep running back Jonathan Taylor. How the Colts' coaching staff uses the three-time Pro Bowl ball-carrier will be fascinating to watch.

Monday Night Football: Los Angeles Chargers at Baltimore Ravens

The Los Angeles Chargers will travel all the way to Baltimore in hopes of finally registering their first win of the season. If they lose, it will be a long trip home after Monday Night Football , with just six days to prepare to host the New York Jets.

Meanwhile, the Ravens should look different during this prime-time affair. Jacoby Brissett is expected to start at quarterback after being acquired via trade from the Arizona Cardinals on Nov. 6.

The 33-year-old is a life preserver to keep the 4-5 Ravens afloat until Lamar Jackson can return late in the season.

articles.title: NFL: Washington Commanders rally to defeat the New York Giants thanks to Jayden Daniels and Stefon Diggs
articles.summary: Stefon Diggs’ late touchdown secured a tense 24-21 Washington Commanders win over the New York Giants after Cam Skattebo had rushed for two touchdowns; Daniels finished with 249 passing yards and three TDs, with Antonio Williams and Ben Sinnott also reaching the end zone
articles.body:
Jayden Daniels threw his third touchdown pass of the game, a 32-yarder to Stefon Diggs with 57 seconds left, as the Washington Commanders rallied to defeat the New York Giants 24-21 in what was essentially a must-win game.

Daniels' connection with Diggs in the final minute came after he threw his first two interceptions of the season to end the previous two drives.

He was 23 of 33 for 249 yards and had TD throws to Ben Sinnott and Antonio Williams while running 10 times for 28 yards.

"You could mess up the whole game but still have a chance to win," said Daniels.

Coming back keeps hope alive for the Commanders (3-5-1), who moved two games back of the NFC East-leading Giants (5-3-1).

"It just gives you confidence we can go out there and compete and we can close out a game versus the top dog," Daniels said.

"Last time we played them it didn't go the way that we wanted to or planned to, so we went out there and we improved from the last time. We responded when we had those moments."

"It's a missed opportunity, certainly, but it doesn't change things for us," Giants coach John Harbaugh said. "There is still a lot of football to play. We played well - just not well enough. We worked hard for this, but you can't let it bring you down. This was one that got away."

JJ McCarthy threw for a career-high 293 yards in his first home start for New York since a trade from Minnesota in late September but was intercepted by Rasul Douglas in the final minute, sending fans to the exit doors.

"It's easy to second-guess the final two passes," McCarthy said. "The pressure was coming. It's one-on-one outside. I wanted to give my playmaker a chance. This football team is going to get better from this. I know it."

articles.title: Steelers should pursue former first-round WR after Eagles release
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers would be wise to pursue former first-round wide receiver Marquise "Hollywood" Brown after his Philadelphia Eagles departure.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles are reportedly waiving a former first-round wide receiver — and the Pittsburgh Steelers should be all over it.

According to NFL insider Jordan Schultz, the Philadelphia Eagles are waiving veteran wide receiver Marquise "Hollywood" Brown after both sides mutually agreed that a split would be "beneficial".

"Sources: The Eagles are waiving WR Marquise 'Hollywood' Brown, as both sides agreed it would be beneficial for all involved," Schultz wrote via X.

Brown, who was drafted by the Baltimore Ravens with the 25th overall pick in the first round of the 2019 NFL Draft, has served as one of the NFL's most underrated deep threats thanks to his game-changing speed. During his eight-year NFL career, Brown has recorded 4,385 receiving yards and 33 touchdowns.

As if the Steelers ' concerning wide receiver room wasn't enough reason to consider signing Brown, Hollywood is also the cousin of former Steeler Antonio Brown, who is regarded as one of the best wide receivers in franchise history.

It remains to be seen if Brown will be picked up on waivers, but if he somehow clears, the Steelers would make for an excellent landing spot given the team's inability to add any talent at the trade deadline.

articles.title: Cowboys’ DeMarvion Overshown trending toward return vs. 49ers after injury update
articles.summary: DeMarvion Overshown is looking for redemption after drawing a puzzling unsportsmanlike penalty during the Dallas Cowboys’ Week 9 win versus the Indianapolis...
articles.body:
DeMarvion Overshown is looking for redemption after drawing a puzzling unsportsmanlike penalty during the Dallas Cowboys ' Week 9 win versus the Indianapolis Colts, and it appears he will get the chance to earn it this Sunday against the San Francisco 49ers. The 2023 third-round draft pick is trending toward playing after posting full practice participation on Thursday, via Clarence Hill Jr.

The Cowboys have a lengthy injury report, but it might get a little lighter come Friday. Overshown has dealt with hamstring and back injuries throughout the 2026 campaign and was inactive for the Colts game. That did not stop him from celebrating a big fumble recovery with his teammates on the field , a rule violation that cost Dallas 15 yards. The 26-year-old linebacker accepted responsibility for the mistake, but he probably still feels inclined to make a grand gesture on the gridiron.

Forcing a turnover of his own or getting a big stop would probably suffice. Overshown has one interception, one forced fumble, 20 combined tackles and two passes defended in three games played. He is in the final year of his contract and is therefore running out of time to drive up his market value and wow executives. An impactful performance versus the 49ers, one of the current favorites to win Super Bowl 61, would surely help his cause.

When in uniform, DeMarvion Overshown can be a positive presence for a run defense that is surrendering an NFC-worst 147.4 yards per week. Barring an unforeseen setback, he will line up opposite the 49ers (7-1) inside AT&T Stadium.

articles.title: Tom Brady Ranks Chicago Bears Above Bills Despite Worse Record
articles.summary: Tom Brady puts the 7-2 Bears at number one in his latest NFL power rankings, citing a unique rule for staying on top while the team heads into a bye week.
articles.body:
Tom Brady has placed the 7-2 Chicago Bears at the top of his latest NFL power rankings, even though the Buffalo Bills and San Francisco 49ers hold better records. The NFL legend explained his logic via Fox Sports after the Bears beat the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. He noted that his list requires a team to lose a game to drop from the first spot.

"Yeah and in my rankings, you got to lose to fall out of the top spot," Brady said. The quarterback admitted that Caleb Williams made things difficult with four interceptions during the recent win, yet Chicago remains number one for now. Brady believes great teams must win ugly sometimes, pointing to how the defense created pressure all night long. He also highlighted Cairo Santos for coming up clutch to win the game in the final seconds.

Brady paused to consider a specific scenario regarding the current schedule. The Bears have not lost since Williams returned from his injury, and now they get a bye week to clean things up. Brady wondered what happens to the number one team when they sit out a week. If the Bears remain inactive, Buffalo could surge to the summit, according to his suggestion that the door might be open. The Bills beat the Minnesota Vikings in Week 9 to earn their spot in second place.

Per Yahoo Sports , the Jaguars took fifth place after going 6-2 following their win over the Baltimore Ravens. Within this specific ranking list, they stand as the sole team boasting six wins to reach the top five. The Denver Broncos hold fourth place at 7-2, while the 49ers come in at third after beating the Las Vegas Raiders.

A report from Windy City Gridiron lists the San Francisco 49ers as the number one team, arguing they have been the league's best since week one. That same source places the Chicago Bears at number two, noting they are the best team if every squad plays its best game. The report emphasizes that Chicago proved it can win even when it does not have its A game, as shown against Tampa.

The Bears are currently in their bye week after securing a 7-2 start to the year. According to Bear Goggles On , the team finds itself in first place in the NFC North despite some ups and downs. The source highlights defensive end Austin Booker as a key winner for the team this season. It also names Kyler Gordon as the Comeback Player of the Year after he racked up 13 tackles and four sacks in four games.

Rookie Dillon Thieneman leads the Bears in tackles with 57, plus five pass deflections and two tackles for loss. The versatile weapon has shown a mix of linebacker and defensive back skills while Coby Bryant sits out. Despite an encouraging Week 9 showing versus the Buccaneers, Jaylon Johnson has allowed a 104.9 passer rating this year. In that specific game, he permitted a 20% completion percentage and saw an interception returned for a touchdown.

With 43.1 net yards per punt, special teams player Tory Taylor holds the 11th rank in the NFL. His longest field goal stands at 65 yards, showing reliability even without much flashiness. On Sunday, November 22, the team will resume play from their bye against the New Orleans Saints. The Saints enter that Week 10 meeting with a 3-5 record ahead of their game against the Carolina Panthers.
